headline: CLAUDE WORKS
WHILE YOU'RE **OUT**
cover.hook_pick_reason: Slides 2-3 back it directly: Duet checks connected accounts every few hours and a virtual machine keeps working when your devices are off. The reader-impact option ('asks first before it pays') is also supported by the guardrails slide but is narrower and could sound like a payments product. The rivalry option rests on AI Times alone and Muse is not the main story. The US-only preview is stated on slide 2.

slides.title: Anthropic's new agent acts in the background
body: Anthropic opened a **research preview** of Claude Duet. It flags work needing attention, does assigned tasks in the background and asks before acting for you.

slides.title: US only, by waitlist
body: Access is by waitlist for **US Claude Pro and Max subscribers**. It is included in those plans and shares their existing usage limits. Readers outside the US cannot sign up yet.

slides.title: A morning brief, then regular check-ins
body: Duet sends a short morning brief from your connected apps and **checks those accounts every few hours**. A virtual machine with its own browser keeps working when your devices are off.

slides.title: It must ask before it acts
body: Duet has to show the action and **wait for you** before sending a message, paying, signing or deleting. Securities trading and transfers between accounts stay **prohibited**.

slides.title: Still early, and a crowded race
body: It may misread threads or rank urgency poorly, and you cannot yet watch its browser. AI Times reports Duet competes with **Meta's Muse** and OpenAI's Dots.

facts.text: Anthropic opened a research preview of Claude Duet, a proactive agent that surfaces work needing attention, carries out assigned tasks in the background, and asks before acting on a user's behalf.
Access is by waitlist for US Claude Pro and Max subscribers; it is included in those plans and shares their existing usage limits.
It sends a concise morning brief based on connected apps and checks those accounts every few hours. A virtual machine with its own browser keeps working when the user's devices are off.
Duet must show the proposed action and wait before sending a message, making a payment, signing a document, or deleting anything; securities trading and transfers between accounts remain prohibited.
The preview remains limited: Duet may misread threads or rank urgency poorly, and users cannot yet view its browser.
It can use more than 6,000 connectors and plugins in the Claude Marketplace, including Gmail, Slack, QuickBooks, Stripe, HubSpot and Shopify.
AI Times reports Duet competes with Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots, and says Duet's difference is that it periodically checks business accounts and flags what needs attention before the user asks.

caption:
Anthropic just launched Claude Duet, an AI agent that works in the background and asks before it acts.

It is a research preview, open by waitlist to US Claude Pro and Max subscribers only.

→ Sends a morning brief and checks your connected accounts every few hours
→ Must show the action and wait for you before sending, paying, signing or deleting
→ Still early: it may misread threads, and you cannot yet watch its browser

Would you let an AI agent check your inbox while you are away?
